collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 6-13 and a fisher or an adult; in the story (name1) was born with a hand that has two fingers)

collection.description: A child born with a two-fingered hand cannot tie the usual fishing knot: let them find another way, or keep trying the usual way.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) was born with one hand that has two fingers, and (subject.he/she) does almost everything with it the same way everyone else does. But the fishing knot (friend) is teaching just won't work: it needs three fingers holding the loop at once. (subject) has tried eleven times. (subject.He/she) is starting to get cross.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) stops showing and says, "Forget my way. How would YOU hold it?" (subject) thinks, tries using (subject.his/her) teeth, then (subject.his/her) knee, then the two fingers in a pinch. On the fifth try, the knot holds, and it's tight. (friend) tests it. It's a perfectly good knot. It's a different way of tying it. By the end of the season, some of the other children are tying it (subject)'s way, because it's faster.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) keeps showing the usual way, slower and slower. (subject) keeps trying. On the twentieth try (subject.he/she) throws the net down and stomps off. Later (friend) finds (subject.him/her) by the canoes, tying the knot perfectly in a way (friend) has never seen before. "I worked it out," says (subject), not looking up. "My way." (friend) sits down and asks to be taught.
